profile_text.body:
Cerence Inc. is a public company headquartered in Burlington, Massachusetts, traded under the ticker CRNC and registered with the SEC under CIK 0001768267. On its own site the company describes itself as delivering conversational and agentic AI-powered user experiences for automotive and beyond, built on CaLLM, which it describes as its family of language models. It says it aims to bring natural, multimodal and safe interactions to the automotive world, and that it is moving to advance generative AI and large language model innovation it believes will be central to the future automotive and transportation user experience.

Among the products described on the site is Cerence Emergency Vehicle Detection, or EVD, which the company says is already deployed in production vehicles. It uses existing vehicle microphones and AI trained to distinguish sirens from traffic, road noise, music and other sounds, and the company says it can detect and localize more than 1,500 emergency sirens across nearly 50 countries, from more than 300 meters away with interior microphones and beyond 800 meters when paired with exterior microphones. The site also describes dynamic speech enhancement for multi-seat in-car environments, allowing passengers in different zones to make requests at the same time, demonstrated by Timo Matheja and Stefan Hamerich. A separate piece on Zero Trust architecture for in-car assistants is credited to Kaivan Karimi, Business Development Senior Director at Cerence AI, and Frank Kaleck, Director Industry Advisory Automotive at Microsoft.

The site reports third quarter results with revenue up 12% year over year and connected services revenue up 20% year over year, along with operating cash flow of $20M supporting a first-ever share repurchase program. No lawsuits involving the company are recorded, and Massachusetts is listed as its jurisdiction.
